description: Hi! We're Sandman, a Jakarta-based team taking on the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. We're passionate about space and education, and want to make space exploration fun and easy for young learners through game-style learning, storytelling, and solid software. Our skills: coding, web & game development, hardware, design, data analysis, writing, education. We speak English and Indonesian.
summary: Homebound is a browser-based space habitat simulation in which players act as Flight Director of an outpost on Mars or the Moon. Players manage closed-loop life support (ECLSS), a Kilopower reactor grid, hydroponic food production, and radiation shielding while guiding three crew specialists until the Earth Return Vehicle (ERV-1) arrives. Each day presents a directive or space weather event whose response has a visible cost. Scientific values are drawn from NASA and CSA public resources and stored as curated constants. Homebound turns this science into decisions: players learn why resource balancing, circadian management, and environmental mitigation matter for survival beyond Earth.
details:
HOMEBOUND: Command a Mars or Moon Habitat Through Real NASA Science

What It Is and How It Works

Homebound is a turn-based habitat command simulation that runs as a lightweight single-page web app. Players act as Flight Director of an outpost on Mars or the Moon and must keep the crew alive until the Earth Return Vehicle (ERV-1) arrives. The Mars Habitat (ARES) mission lasts 30 days. The Lunar Outpost (ARTEMIS) mission lasts 45 days and includes 14 consecutive nights of total darkness. Each Sol (day) follows this loop:

  • Morning Telemetry Briefing: Players review live habitat metrics: cabin oxygen (ECLSS), food rations, hull shield integrity, crew stamina and mood, and power distribution across five subsystems (Life Support, Greenhouse, Dome Shields, Radar/Comms, Science Lab).
  • Daily Directives and Space Weather Events: Players choose one of three responses to each scenario. Examples include calibrating MOXIE oxygen production, adjusting habitat lighting to 480 nm to reduce circadian disruption, or moving the crew to a shelter before a coronal mass ejection (CME) arrives. Every option shows its resource costs and benefits before the player commits. The Mars campaign has 30 directives, and the lunar campaign has 26.
  • Night Rest and Regeneration: Crew recover stamina as long as oxygen and food stay above 30%. The Sabatier loop recycles oxygen (+4%), while thermal stress wears down the structure (-2%).
  • Outcome: Surviving to Day 30 triggers the ERV-1 arrival. If critical life support reaches zero, containment fails.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Learning through consequence: The game includes 8 curated NASA educational insight cards. Each appears when the player’s situation matches its topic, such as MOXIE oxygen extraction or Sabatier propellant production. Players see why closed-loop recycling and radiation shielding matter because their decisions affect the mission.
  • Bilingual access: The full interface, including directives, space weather events, glossary, and tutorials, is available in English and Indonesian.
  • Zero-friction access: No downloads, installation, or API keys. It runs in desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers.
  • Intended impact: We aim to help young learners understand why life support, radiation protection, and resource balancing matter for survival beyond Earth. Target players are Indonesian students aged 13 to 20. Impact has not yet been measured formally.

Tools and Technology

  • Languages and architecture: Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules) with a modular component and SPA router structure
  • Rendering: Phaser 3 (v3.90) for the planetary stage, telemetry HUD, and animated scenes
  • Motion: GSAP (GreenSock) for viewport transitions, orbital motion, and reticle controls
  • Styling: A custom CSS design system following NASA Space Apps Challenge branding (Blue Yonder #2E96F5, Electric Blue #0042A6, Neon Yellow #EAFE07), with Fira Code and Fira Sans loaded from Google Fonts
  • Audio: A procedural synthesizer built on the Web Audio API generates ambient drones, clicks, radar pings, and alarms in real time, with no audio files
  • Graphics: Sprites, module textures, and spacecraft are drawn procedurally on Canvas 2D at runtime. The planet backgrounds use NASA reference images.
  • Build: Vite 8, producing a client bundle of [about 520 KB gzipped, confirm with npm run build]
  • Data sources: NASA DONKI, OSDR (OSD-128, OSD-379, OSD-412, OSD-665), RadLab, Mars Trek, and the Canadian Space Agency food production toolkit. Values are stored as curated constants and are not queried live.
  • Hardware: Developed on [laptop or PC and OS]. Tested on [browsers and devices].

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of presenting space data as charts or quizzes, Homebound makes the science part of the gameplay. A CME warning forces a choice between sheltering the crew and keeping systems running, and the cost of that choice appears in the next morning’s briefing. Players learn the science because they have to act on it under time pressure.

Key Design Considerations

  • Mathematical transparency: Every preview shows exact, deterministic changes, so there are no hidden penalties.
  • Inclusivity: WCAG AA contrast, dyslexia-friendly monospace telemetry tags, and layouts that adapt to touch and mouse.
  • Respectful educational pacing: NASA Science Fact drawers appear for quick insight and can be toggled off without breaking immersion.

AI Disclosure

Parts of the code were developed with AI assistance (vibe coding) and reviewed by our team.
